chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked: A man who performs Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) and has his own clothes in his pouch; should he sell some of his clothes to buy a sacrificial animal (Hady)? He (AS) said: No. This is among that with which the believer adorns himself; he fasts, and he does not take from his clothes anything.
And the Hady suffices for the obligatory sacrifice and for the voluntary Udhiyah; he narrated that.
ai.seo_question: Should a pilgrim sell their clothes to buy the Hajj sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the personal garments worn during the state of Ihram are considered part of the pilgrim's adornment (Zinah) and thus should not be liquidated to purchase the Hady, preserving the dignity of the ritual. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the Hady offered during Tamattu' Hajj is sufficient to discharge both the obligatory sacrifice of Hajj and the voluntary Eid al-Adha sacrifice, eliminating the need for a separate offering.
